claims.claim: Reviewers report that the user interface features tiny fonts or reversed size settings that make it difficult to read or adjust.

citations.review_text: Very fun city builder type game in an medieval detailed settings.  Only issue is the UI interface size setting is reversed 0.75 is large and 1+ is small.

TL;DR: Overpriced for amount of gameplay and features. THE UI is horrendous. It a good very basic micro-managing city builder.  DO NOT BUY UNLESS ON SALE FOR $5

The Good: If you would like to try a game that is a micro-managing your city builder, which is fun, then this is the game for you. Its very rudimentary and enjoyable. Especially when your population experiences mass growth. That is a fun hurdle to manage. There is a tutorial and then the game. Its basic, and a great way to explore this genre DEPENDING ON THE PRICE.

The bad: THE UI is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious. You can have a building in nearly permanent limbo no matter how many laborers and builders you assign to the task. The prioritize feature is the most useless button Ive seen in a non early access game. I cannot describe to you how annoying the priority system in this game is. It can tank your game if you need food supply and the builders just refuse to build the location or upgrade a house. I should be able to make it the civilization, as a whole, their number 1 priority. Like to the point where the prioritize building this over eating and they die.  LASTLY the price is way too high. this is not worth $20USD. Ive played better games for longer for half of that. if you catch it on sale for $5 then you can pick it up.
Good game with a learning curve, but so far it;s going great. I only had to start over 3 times. AND Please fix the TINY lettering font on the info and charts. It is impossible to see.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks a tutorial covering its complexity, leaving players to figure out systems through trial and error.

citations.review_text: The tutorials are very fast and after you finish them there is very little direction given to you on how to proceed. I have played further and you can figure it out just trying different things. I am actually making some progress now, and I find myself enjoying the challenge.

nice cozy colony sim game, simple enough to follow once you get the hang of it, unless it's changed from when i started years ago, game lacks a tutorial but the sink or swim approach I actually appreciate as it gives you a great incentive to learn and meet your peoples needs to make a thriving colony.

Too easy to lose where you are in the game. It therefore becomes very hard to stick to a plan and you instead start over repeatedly.

Graphics aren't so good now, though they were good for when the game was released.

Doesn't provide a tutorial if I remember correctly, or just doesn't cover the complexity of the game. 

In short: overwhelming and unengaging.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience sudden societal collapses and population die-offs from starvation and freezing despite having established food and resource production.

citations.review_text: I started a town 6 times and the people died out from  under me to the point where the society stalled. They died of freezing in the summer. They died of starvation while harvesting full fields of food. All efforts to feed the little bas**rds had no effect. It's a fun concept and I was engaged, but I ground down to the easiest level, best weather, and no disasters, and still had societal collapse. I have more important things to fail at.

Good game, can be difficult
Love the surprises of thinking everything is going well, and then all the villagers die from starvation or freezing within a few minutes.

Just no.
It's one of those games where if you dare to go 10x speed for 10 seconds, your population starts starving and dying even though you have a maxed number of:
1) Hunters (elks walking in their faces)
2) Gatherers
3) Fishermen (2 docks)
4) Farmers (3 farm fields)

Your population of 22 will still starve and die. 
I wanted to be sure, so I have reloaded that save and tried to optimize as best as I can, but, no, apparently:
8 fishermen
3 Hunters
3 Farmers
2 Gatherers
All fairly close to each other

Will not be enough to feed a village of 22 individuals.

No wonder the most basic achievement of this game has only 20%, this game is utterly unbalanced.

And plus...nothing really happens during the city building...no events, no story line, nothing. 
Your buildings can't be powered up.
No technology tree.
It's just you in a sandbox. 
Man, the sadness.

citations.review_text:
Pretty adictive. Cool game.
However, there is not that much to do. After you succeed with the main part of the game, which is getting enough food, resources, tools, happy and healthy vilagers and mainly positive population growth, then there is nothing else to do. You just keep growing, with some random events from time to time. You will get more people, so you will have to get more resources and houses. That's all.  It would be good to have good music to carry you during game...but it's meh.

There is not much of interest of how people live or anything. Endless building. It was fun, I liked it, but after some time you will get bored, when you have no goal.

It's a cool game, but most people won't play it more than I did as it doesn't have much content. It's definitely NOT worth 19€ for this reason, unless you really come to like the mods which aren't many or groundbreaking frankly speaking.

A very strange city builder. It's angling for hardcore realism, where your colony could be wiped out by disease, famine, or inclement weather, but in reality none of those things happened. In my one and only 8hr run, I reached a point where my 3rd generation didn't have enough children, so all of my carefully built infrastructure was eventually manned by a skeleton crew as the elderly died off and we waited for people to breed. And that's all I could do: wait. I was never in danger of having the settlement dwindle away to nothing; our educated populace were drowning in food, everyone lived in warm stone houses, the church and tavern kept everyone disgustingly happy, and we wanted for nothing from the trader.

Unfortunately I've just listed almost all the mechanics in base game Banished, and that's why I feel I can write down my thoughts after just one run. I reached a point early on where all the most ambitious projects were finished, and a stable equilibrium was reached. The downfall of my run came because young couples did not have any empty houses to move into to start a family (although they were happy to live in shared houses...) - and once I realised this the problem was solved, but I still faced a decade long wait to salvage the situation. There isn't much to do in between crises - everything ticks along by itself, and crucially you don't have any control over your townspeople. I can't assign villagers a house to live, or a specific job, and there is no other customization or specialization beyond this. The result of this is that when I switched the weighting of jobs, for example increasing the amount of farmers in spring and autumn to sow and harvest the fields, a random villager would be assigned. This sounds innocuous, but you lose a noticeable amount of efficiency if your villager lives far away from their job - they have to walk to work, walk back home when they get hungry, walk back home when they get cold, walk back to deposit resources, and so on. The…

citations.review_text: Banished is a fun game, but the building inventory system is frustrating. Whenever you open a building’s inventory, it either scrolls down automatically or won’t let you scroll at all.

Still amazing in 2026, a sequel would be nice though. Get this game on sale. Has steam workshop, go grab an extra large map mod. People still play this. Bare to no bugs, except a mouse scrolling bug that can be easily worked around.

Everything takes careful planning and moderation, but it allows for many different strategies and configurations with the base elements of the game. Mechanics are simple, but interact with complex interdependency.

I want to give a neutral rating, but that's not an option unfortunately.

The overall mechanics of the game is easy. But there is no tutorial, so you will have to learn them yourself.

7. Also, it would have been nice if the citizens can just do their jobs without unnecessary interruptions. For example, i would see them gather woods, then put the woods to the stock pile, then pause, then pick it up again and put it to the construction…

citations.review_text: It took me 20 hours and 5 worlds to get the first achievement. Tornado took down almost every non-food-related structure and left me with only 1 sheep, so my people froze to death due to a lack of fuel. I expected the sheep to reproduce by mitosis, but the miracle never happened. Also, in my current village, some people are getting kicked out of their houses. Apparently, they are getting so depressed that they refuse to move into the boarding house and choose to starve to death instead. Great game 10/10.

Started a new game on easy mode, built up my food sources and got my settlement established with a population starting to boom. 30 minutes in and half of the settlement and population gets flattened by a tornado. 10/10 Banished experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the base game as lacking clear long-term goals, milestones, or an extensive endgame.

citations.review_text:
[h2]PRO[/h2]
[list]
[*]Brutal but fair difficulty, one bad winter and you feel it
[*]No hand holding, you actually have to think about your resource chain
[*]Mod support is great if you want more content after the base game
[/list]

[h2]CON[/h2]
[list]
[*]Not much of a "goal" in the base game, no real endgame or milestones
[/list]

[h2]The review[/h2]
I've put hours into this, so yeah I like this game. There isn't really a story here, it's more about the moments you make yourself. Like the winter my firewood stockpile ran out because I didn't plan the distance to the forest properly, or the time my blacksmith had no iron left and half my tools just started breaking one after another. Every town you build turns into its own little disaster story, and that's honestly the appeal.

For the achievement hunters, getting 100% takes a while and some of it is just surviving long enough with specific conditions, so be ready to restart a few times.

If you liked SimCity or Anno but always felt they were a bit too forgiving, Banished will happily make you pay for your mistakes.

Nothing scratches the city builder itch like Banished. There's a reason it inspired just about every city builder that came out since its release 10+ years ago, and there's a reason people still play it today, despite all those similar games that have come out since. If you like sandbox(ish) games, resource management, and watching a city grow, Banished will quickly become your go-to comfort game. 

If you're looking for something with clearly defined progression (technology trees, policies, concrete goals, etc), you will, tbh, probably hate it. Banished is very open ended; the only limits placed on expansion are the resources you have at any given time. This is something a lot of people love about the game, I could also see it being a drawback for some. 

You'll need mods to keep things interesting long term, but there's a great community around Banished with plenty to offer. 

One of my all time favorites (check the playtime), highly recommend.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features no combat or military elements, focusing entirely on peaceful resource management and environmental survival.

citations.review_text:
I honestly can't recommend Banished enough. It's one of those games that proves you don't need flashy graphics or constant action to keep you hooked. The whole game revolves around building a settlement from a small group of exiles, and every decision you make matters. Expand too quickly and you'll run out of food. Forget about firewood before winter and your people freeze. Lose too many workers and your entire town can slowly collapse. What I love most is that there are no enemies to fight or quests telling you what to do. The challenge comes entirely from your own planning and problem-solving. Every new town feels different, and watching a tiny village grow into a thriving community is incredibly rewarding. It's also the kind of game where you keep telling yourself, "Just one more year," and before you know it, hours have disappeared.

If you're into city builders, survival management, or games that reward careful planning, Banished is absolutely worth picking up. Even though it's been around for years, it's still one of the best colony management games ever made and has a timeless feel that keeps me coming back.

My rating: 10/10 – an absolute classic that every colony-building fan should experience.

Ultimate ultimate game
Was recommended to me as I got a Definitive Edition of AoE, but told a friend I love econ, not the war part. 
He told me I am playing the wrong game
If you are addicted to stress, this is the game for you

Addictive Colony Builder with a (sometimes) Unique Soundtrack. It checks every box of a good colony simulator, minus the combat portion. The only combat is the environment and disease ridden flora, fauna, or nomads.

8.75/10 - Runs on pretty much any PC with a pulse, offers a lot of value with seed-map generation.
Turn on some SimCity2000 soundtracks and enjoy. Fun city-builder for those that do not like the military/fighting aspect that other similar-era builders tend to favor.

This is my favourite city builder/surval game.
What I like about it the most is that I can have a relaxing time just creating my village without the worry of raiders or battles. 
Even though I have gained 100% achievements I keep coming back to this game because it's my go to game for when I simply want to chill out.
I wish there were more games like this.

[h2]The review[/h2]
I've put hours into this, so yeah I like this game. There isn't really a story here, it's more about the moments you make yourself. Like the winter my firewood stockpile ran out because I didn't plan the distance to the forest properly, or the time my blacksmith had no iron left and half my tools just started breaking one after another. Every town you build turns into its own little disaster story, and that's honestly the appeal.

For the achievement hunters, getting 100% takes a while and some of it is just surviving long enough with specific conditions, so be ready to restart a few times.

If you liked SimCity or Anno but always felt they were a bit too forgiving, Banished will happily make you pay for your mistakes.

Definitely a game with a bit of a learning curve, dealing with resource management and population collapse. It's very fun and rewarding, plus lots of mods when you get bored of the base game. Sometimes the terrain can be a bit wonky but it's the price you pay for seeded map gen

Ever since release and to this day Banished remains my favorite city builder out there. There's just nothing quite like this one for me.
tl:dr It's a solid 8.5/10 from me

The game drops you in with a few recently exiled people and some supplies, maybe some houses and livestock depending on your difficulty setting, the objective is to build a thriving town in the wilderness you've been dumped into. It's complex to start and has a fairly steep learning curve, your first towns aren't likely to make it very much further than year 100, and getting beyond year 200 is a real challenge, at least until you get a few towns under your belt and learn how to achieve infinite supplies by abusing the trading system. 

Much of my recent experience with Banished was wrapping up all the challenge runs in the achievements, which is why I get into specifics with certain mechanics below. The game is very good and I highly recommend playing it without touching guides or attempting the challenge run achievements for your first few towns. The challenge runs taught me a lot about the game's mechanics, but get frustrating if you try to do multiple in one go. Mountainmen/Uneducated (likely others) at the same time is possible, however.

Most of the systems in the game aren't so deep that you get totally lost in them, save for the graphs menu which is simply mesmerizing, most menus rarely go beyond 1-2 layers in depth which helps quite a lot as you start learning what to pay attention to and what can be ignored. Where the magic really happens, I think, is how these systems play off each other. Usually to the player's detriment, an uneducated citizen works half as fast using twice as many resources, so things like food harvests, construction, tool and clothes crafting, et al, all get affected. 

People start getting sick easier because clothes aren't being made fast enough, tool shortages become more likely as mines dry up faster, tools drying up makes the already slower crop harvesting time b…

Banished is one of those games that quietly sucks you in- and then humbles you real fast.
At first glance, it looks like a simple city-builder. You start with a small group of exiles trying to survive in a new land, and your goal is to help them build a thriving settlement. But very quickly, you realize this isn't about rapid expansion, its about survival, planning, and tough decisions.
What makes Banished stand out is how unforgiving it can be in the best way. Every choice matters. If you over-expand, your people might starve. If you don't prepare for winter, you could loose half your population. Take in too many Nomads, your people will starve quickly. There's a constant tension between growing your town and making sure everyone stays alive, which keeps you fully engaged the entire time. 
I really enjoyed playing at a slower pace. Watching your villagers go about their daily routines like gathering food, building homes, raising families, makes the world feel alive. When things go well, its rewarding. When they don't, you learn quickly not to do that again. Or go back to your last save and start again. I also love the rusticness of the game. Its not flashy and fits the tone perfectly. 
Banished is a deeply satisfying game if you enjoy strategy, resource management, and a bit of a challenge.
Very fun game that punishes you for not paying attention or being greedy. Make sure you have plenty of food on hand!

citations.review_text:
Addictive Colony Builder with a (sometimes) Unique Soundtrack. It checks every box of a good colony simulator, minus the combat portion. The only combat is the environment and disease ridden flora, fauna, or nomads.

8.75/10 - Runs on pretty much any PC with a pulse, offers a lot of value with seed-map generation.

First off this game is very easy to run on most systems. Its a very lightweight game and does not often have any issues. The game has a learning curve, which is an appreciated challenge. It is very fun figuring out how to balance the numbers in your game and not kill everyone. Definitely easier said than done. The mods are also great and easy to work with. I recommend produce storage mods to start.
This is a relaxing city builder game. Its all about the food though, your people will die fast with out food. Graphics are good, no stress on your PC.
